target.title: feat: add Control UI plugin management
target.body: Closes #103135 ## What Problem This Solves OpenClaw's optional plugins are discoverable and manageable through CLI/config workflows, but the Control UI had no coherent place to see what is installed and running, enable a bundled capability such as Workboard, install or remove a ClawHub plugin, or connect lightweight MCP-based integrations. ## Why This Change Was Made This builds a full plugin manager at `/settings/plugins` on top of the existing plugin lifecycle, with two tabs: - **Installed** — the complete local inventory (141 plugins on a real gateway) grouped by category, flowing into two columns on wide layouts. A compact **inventory pulse** replaces stat cards: a segmented enabled/disabled/issues meter whose legend and counts live inside the filter chips. Every row opens a **detail overlay** (hero art, primary enable/install action, metadata table); an overflow (`…`) menu offers Enable/Disable, View details, and a confirm-guarded **Remove** for externally installed plugins. The tab also manages **MCP servers** inline (list, add via URL or command with inferred transport, enable/disable, remove) through the existing `config.patch` seam using minimal RFC 7396 merge patches; stdio rows show only the command since args can carry credentials. - **Discover** — the store: featured bundled plugins, official externals, and a **"Connect your world"** shelf of 28 connectors organized into use-case groups (Work & productivity, Coding & infrastructure, Home & media, Everyday life). One-click MCP connectors cover Notion, Linear, Todoist, Airtable, Canva, Stripe, GitHub, Sentry, Context7, DeepWiki, Hugging Face, and Home Assistant; curated ClawHub searches cover calendar, email, PDF, transcription, Jira, Grafana, Kubernetes, Spotify, Sonos, Reddit, stocks, flights, news, maps, translation, and notes. Typing in the search box queries ClawHub inline (through the gateway — anonymous, no account needed) and appends a **From ClawHub** section with download counts and source-verification badges; "Browse ClawHub" is a quiet header link there. Every catalog entry renders **cover art**: 172 bundled 512px WebP illustrations (generated with Codex CLI, ~2.1MB under `ui/public/plugin-art/`) covering the full bundled inventory, every connector, and the store shelves, with deterministic gradient monogram tiles as the fallback for unknown ClawHub packages. The gateway CSP is `img-src 'self'`, so artwork ships with the bundle. **Connector vetting.** Every connector passed a three-stage subagent review: (1) official-docs verification plus live endpoint probes for MCP servers, (2) ClawHub result-quality and malware/typosquat screening for curated searches, and (3) an adversarial pass that dynamically registered OAuth clients to prove one-click viability. That review removed Figma (client-allowlisted registration, live 403) and Atlassian (upstream OAuth issuer-mismatch bug), downgraded GitHub to PAT-based setup (no dynamic client registration upstream), fixed the Linear endpoint (`/sse` retired → `/mcp`) and Home Assistant (`/api/mcp`, streamable HTTP), and dropped or retargeted searches whose top results were squatted by suspicious packages (a bulk-published wrapper cluster routing queries and API keys to a third-party service now sits on ClawHub's "never highlight" radar; details in the review artifacts). Backend additions (all additive, no protocol version bump): - `plugins.uninstall` (`operator.admin`, control-plane write): lock-guarded removal mirroring the CLI flow — config references, install record, managed files, registry refresh. Bundled plugins stay disable-only. - `PluginCatalogEntry` gains `category` (manifest-derived) and `removable`; search results gain `downloads` and `verificationTier`. - Catalog display metadata prefers manifest names/channel labels/blurbs over npm package specifiers ("Telegram — simplest way to get started…" instead of "@openclaw/telegram"). - Hosted feed entries without a declared runtime id no longer pin `expectedPluginId` to their package name (which rejected every legitimate install), while explicitly declared ids stay enforced even when they equal the package name; installed packages now also suppress their hosted catalog rows. ## User Impact Operator admins get a single place to see what is installed and running, click into any plugin for details, enable/disable/remove via familiar store-style menus, install from the curated store or inline ClawHub search, and wire up vetted MCP connectors without touching JSON. Read-only operators can still browse and search with mutation controls disabled and explained. ## Evidence - `pnpm tsgo:all`, `pnpm test:ui` (i18n drift gate + 2,693 UI tests across 188 files), focused backend suites (protocol validators, management service incl. uninstall/removable/pin regression tests, gateway handlers, descriptor scopes), and the 3-scenario Chromium E2E all pass on Blacksmith Testbox. - The E2E covers the detail overlay, menu-driven enable and uninstall with confirm + page notice, unified inline ClawHub search with badges, connector cards, risk-ack retry, read-only blocking, list-failure retry, and mobile layout. - `pnpm build` passes including the production Control UI build; protocol schema/Swift generators are deterministic. - **Live gateway proof** (isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + sanitized env, this branch's build): browsed the 141-plugin inventory, installed `@openclaw/bluebubbles` from ClawHub through the UI and removed it via the menu flow, and added/removed MCP connectors with the config file verified after each step. - Mandatory autoreview (Codex, gpt-5.5, high) ran across four iterations; accepted findings — MCP transport defaults, RFC 7396 delete semantics, a runtime-id pin regression, duplicate hosted catalog rows after install, and Discover-tab error visibility — were each fixed with regression tests. Final run clean. ### Screenshots (live gateway, this branch) #### Installed inventory: pulse header, two columns, full artwork (dark) ![Installed inventory](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/pr-103176/installed-dark.png) ![Inventory artwork](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/pr-103176/installed-artwork-dark.png) ![Row actions menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/pr-103176/row-menu-dark.png) #### Plugin detail overlay ![Detail overlay](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/pr-103176/detail-dark.png) #### Discover: featured shelf + grouped connectors (full page) ![Discover full](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/pr-103176/discover-full-dark.png) #### Unified inline ClawHub search ![Unified search](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/pr-103176/unified-search-dark.png) #### Light theme ![Installed light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/pr-103176/installed-light.png) ![Discover light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/pr-103176/discover-light.png) #### Mobile

target.title: fix(tasks): normalize legacy delivery status
target.body:
## Summary

- normalize legacy task sidecar `not-requested` delivery statuses to the canonical `not_applicable` value during import
- repair already-migrated shared-state rows on database open so affected upgrades recover without manual SQL
- make strict atomic restore failures diagnosable without changing the no-throw boundary
- cover fresh sidecar migration, existing shared SQLite state, and parser-error logging

## Issue / Motivation

Closes #103168.

A task sidecar produced by an older release can contain `delivery_status = 'not-requested'`. The shared task registry only accepts `not_applicable`, so preserving the old value causes one row to abort restoration of the whole registry and makes linked TaskFlows appear to reference missing tasks.

## What Problem This Solves

Users upgrading from affected releases can have valid task rows stranded in shared SQLite under an obsolete delivery-status spelling. This change canonicalizes future imports and idempotently repairs existing shared-state rows before task restoration, preventing a single legacy value from making the durable task registry unavailable. If another invalid persisted value still blocks strict atomic restore, the warning now includes the formatted parser error so operators can diagnose the row value while the registry remains empty.

## Changes

- map `not-requested` to `not_applicable` at the legacy sidecar import boundary
- update matching existing `task_runs` rows in the additive shared-state migration transaction
- format caught task-registry restore errors before logging them
- add regression coverage for both migration paths and restore-error diagnostics

## Testing

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-state-migrations.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts` — 3 files passed, 127 tests passed
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/tasks/task-registry.ts src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts` — passed
- `pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --type-check --deny-warnings src/tasks/task-registry.ts src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `git diff --check` — passed

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

The affected-installation report provides redacted, real upgrade evidence from OpenClaw `2026.6.10` to `2026.6.11`: five persisted rows contained `not-requested`, the database passed `PRAGMA integrity_check`, and the task registry failed to restore. After backing up the database and applying the same exact normalization implemented here, `not-requested` → `not_applicable`, restart restored the registry, removed the false missing-linked-task TaskFlow findings, and `openclaw tasks audit --json` completed normally. See the issue's **Observed state** and **Verified workaround** sections: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/103168

### Automated regression evidence

- the sidecar regression fixture starts with `delivery_status = 'not-requested'` and verifies the loaded task exposes `deliveryStatus: 'not_applicable'`
- the shared-state regression test seeds the obsolete value directly, reopens the database without a legacy sidecar, and verifies the stored value is repaired to `not_applicable`
- the logging regression makes `loadSnapshot()` throw the exact invalid-value parser error, verifies the warning contains that value, and confirms strict restore leaves the registry empty
- current-main overlap check: a local no-commit merge against current `main` completed without conflicts; no branch refresh is claimed
- pre-refresh focused validation on `c1911606c7f22f4b688ff03f0abd71e852e1b802`: 3 files and 127 tests passed; oxfmt, type-aware oxlint, diff check, and secret scan passed
- local post-refresh test execution was not claimed because this worktree had no `node_modules`; CI performs the exact-head run

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value cron.sessionRetention to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `cron.sessionRetention: "0h"` (or `"0d"`, `"0ms"`) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. Unlike `heartbeat.every` — where `"0m"` is the documented disable sentinel with a runtime `ms <= 0` guard in `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs` — `cron.sessionRetention` uses `false` (boolean) to disable and `resolveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` directly with no guard. `sweepCronRunSessions` then computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all cron run sessions for immediate deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `superRefine` only checks whether `parseDurationMs` throws — treating any non-throwing return value (including `0`) as valid. `parseDurationMs` itself returns `0` for zero inputs (not an error), and `resolveRetentionMs` does not defend against it. The positivity gate belongs in schema validation where config-level diagnostics surface the misconfiguration before runtime damage.

## User Impact

An operator who accidentally sets `cron.sessionRetention: "0h"` (e.g. mistyping `"24h"`) will see all cron run sessions immediately deleted on the next sweep cycle with no error. After this fix, the misconfiguration is caught at config load time with a clear diagnostic. The documented disable path (`false`) is unaffected.

## Evidence

- **Claim proved**: `cron.sessionRetention` rejects zero intervals (non-documented paths) while accepting positive intervals and `false` (documented disable).
- **Current head**: `e78e3377739eb180fb7ca36372964e18ff4af3a8`.
- **Commands / artifacts**:
  - `node --import tsx` runtime bug proof (before fix)
  - `pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json` (after fix)
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/schema.test.ts`
  - `git diff --check`

### Runtime bug proof (before fix — `resolveRetentionMs` returns 0ms)

```text
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { resolveRetentionMs } from './src/cron/session-reaper.ts';
console.log(resolveRetentionMs({sessionRetention: '0h'}));
"
0
```

`0ms` → `cutoff = now - 0 = now` → all cron run sessions immediately deleted.

### After fix: zero values rejected by config validation

```text
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "cron.sessionRetention",
      "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 24h"
    }
  ]
}
```

### After fix: positive intervals still accepted

```text
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### After fix: `false` (documented disable) unaffected

Config `cron: { sessionRetention: false }` continues to disable pruning as documented in `docs/cli/cron.md`.

### Focused Vitest

1 test file, 59 tests passed (3 new + 56 existing unaffected).

### Diff whitespace checks

`git diff --check` passed.

- **Not tested / proof gaps**: None.

target.title: Add 1Password SecretRef plugin
target.body:
## Summary

- Adds a bundled `1password` plugin that provides a managed SecretRef exec provider for 1Password.
- Resolves SecretRefs through the official 1Password CLI (`op`) using service account or Connect auth env, while keeping resolved secrets out of OpenClaw config.
- Adds `openclaw 1password status` and `openclaw 1password setup` helpers for local and server workflows.
- Documents direct-host and container runtime requirements, including the fact that the plugin is bundled but the `op` CLI remains a runtime dependency.

## Linked context

Companion to the bundled Vault SecretRef plugin work in #89255, adding the same plugin-managed SecretRef provider pattern for 1Password.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: OpenClaw can configure and use the bundled `1password` SecretRef provider to resolve model provider credentials from 1Password without storing plaintext provider keys in OpenClaw config.
- Real environment tested: local Podman OpenClaw container using the bundled `1password` extension, a mounted OpenClaw data volume, a maintainer-provided 1Password service account token, and default vault `openclaw`.
- Secret material handling: the service account token and resolved provider credentials were not printed. Status output reports only whether auth env is present.
- Exact setup behavior observed: the container image staged a Linux `op` binary from `docker.io/1password/op:2`, validated it with `2.34.1`, and started the Gateway with `CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP=/home/node/.openclaw/bin/op-wrapper`.
- Evidence after fix: the `onepassword` provider was configured as a plugin-managed exec provider; the runtime saw the `op` wrapper; service account auth was present; the default vault was set.

From local run:

```json
{
  "providerAlias": "onepassword",
  "provider": {
    "configured": true,
    "source": "exec",
    "pluginIntegration": {
      "pluginId": "1password",
      "integrationId": "onepassword"
    }
  },
  "opCommand": "/home/node/.openclaw/bin/op-wrapper",
  "opCommandAvailable": true,
  "authMode": "service-account",
  "hasServiceAccountToken": true,
  "hasConnectHost": false,
  "hasConnectToken": false,
  "defaultVault": "openclaw"
}
```
and 

```
$ openclaw secrets audit --allow-exec
│
◇

OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (unknown) — Hot reload for config, cold sweat for deploys.

Secrets audit: findings. plaintext=1, unresolved=0, shadowed=0, legacy=0.
- [PLAINTEXT_FOUND] /home/node/.openclaw/openclaw.json:gateway.auth.token gateway.auth.token is stored as plaintext.
```

- Proof limitations or environment constraints: this proof used local Podman deployment. The `op` binary is intentionally not bundled into the plugin package; direct users and custom container images must provide a compatible 1Password CLI in the Gateway runtime.

## Tests and validation

Commands run locally:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/1password/src/cli.test.ts extensions/1password/index.test.ts extensions/1password/src/secret-ref-resolver.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:extensions
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/1password
pnpm plugins:inventory:check
node --check extensions/1password/onepassword-secret-ref-resolver.js
git diff --check
```

CLI smoke checks:

```bash
pnpm openclaw 1password --help
pnpm openclaw 1password status --json
pnpm openclaw 1password setup --plan-out /tmp/openclaw-1password-cli-smoke.json --anthropic-id op://openclaw/Anthropic/credential
```

Notes:

- `openclaw 1password --help` correctly reports that the bundled plugin must be enabled first with `openclaw plugins enable 1password`, matching the Vault plugin behavior.
- The setup smoke generated a `secrets apply` plan containing a plugin-managed `onepassword` exec provider and a model provider SecretRef target.

Regression coverage added:

- Resolver tests for manifest integration metadata, inline test values, native `op://` references, shorthand references with `CLAW_1PASSWORD_VAULT`, missing CLI diagnostics, and `CLAW_1PASSWORD_VALUES_JSON` not being passed through the manifest.
- CLI tests for setup plan generation, custom provider mapping, duplicate provider rejection, and traversal segment rejection.
- Plugin entry test for the lazy root CLI registration.

What failed before this fix:

- OpenClaw had the SecretRef provider contract but no bundled 1Password reference implementation.
- Operators had to configure a manual exec provider or external plugin wiring rather than using a bundled plugin-managed provider.

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? `Yes`
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? `Yes`
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? `Yes`
- Highest-risk area: SecretRef resolution shells out to `op`, and the Gateway runtime must provide a trustworthy 1Password CLI plus scoped 1Password auth env.
- Risk mitigation: the provider is opt-in, the CLI surface requires `openclaw plugins enable 1password`, resolver execution is plugin-managed through manifest metadata, secret values are returned only through the SecretRef protocol, setup writes SecretRefs rather than plaintext, tests cover resolver and CLI plan behavior, and docs call out host/container `op` runtime requirements.

## Current review state

Next action: maintainer/security review for the bundled exec resolver trust model and runtime `op` dependency.

Reviewer focus:

- SecretRef provider manifest shape and plugin-managed exec integration.
- 1Password id formats: native `op://<vault>/<item>/<field>`, `<vault>/<item>/<field>`, `<vault>/<item>/<section>/<field>`, and `<item>/<field>` with `CLAW_1PASSWORD_VAULT`.
- Bundled plugin exec resolver trust model: standard 1Password env is passed through, `CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP` can pin the CLI path, and failures avoid printing secret values.
- Docs clarity for direct host usage, service environments, and container images that must provide a Linux `op` binary.

target.title: fix: preserve tools when local-model lean agents use provider overrides
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running an agent with `experimental.localModelLean=true` could lose the expected tool surface when overriding that agent to a non-local provider model.

In the observed failure, a fresh `main` session using `meta/muse-spark-1.1` returned `Tool exec not found`. The same fresh session worked after disabling `main.experimental.localModelLean`, which isolated the failure to local-model lean being applied outside its intended scope.

## Why This Change Was Made

`localModelLean` is intended for local coding-model runs. It was being resolved from agent/session config alone, so a non-local provider override could inherit local-model-specific tool filtering and Tool Search defaults.

This change makes local-model lean model-aware. It keeps the existing behavior for local model providers such as Ollama and llama.cpp, while preventing lean mode from applying to non-local provider overrides when runtime model context is available.

This does not change configured tool policy, session authorization, or static provider catalog metadata handling.

## User Impact

Users can keep `experimental.localModelLean=true` on local-model-oriented agents without accidentally applying that lean tool surface to cloud/provider overrides.

Local-model optimization remains available for local providers, while non-local providers keep their expected direct tool surface.

Closes #102911

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord reasoning messages that wrap content in `_…_` would corrupt markdown code fences and inline code when the message was split across chunks. After a chunk boundary that started with a backtick, the italics rebalancer prepended `_`, producing broken fences such as `_```python` that Discord no longer renders as code.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rebalanceReasoningItalics` already skipped reopening italics when the next chunk already started with `_`. It now also skips when the next chunk starts with a backtick, so fenced and inline code at chunk boundaries stay intact. One backtick check covers triple fences, quad fences, and inline code.

## User Impact

Discord reasoning/thinking replies that contain code blocks or inline code no longer have broken markdown fences when the channel chunks the message.

target.title: Recover stranded message-tool finals by default
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #85714 for the direct/source-channel failure where an agent turn can finish successfully with a substantive final answer, but the user sees nothing because the channel is in `message_tool_only` visible-reply mode and the model skipped `message(action=send)`.

This supersedes #88992. I kept the useful shape from that PR: substantive-final detection, room-event and send-policy guards, a one-shot retry marker, message-tool retry, collect isolation, deferred drain, QA coverage, and clearer prompt wording. The replacement removes the new `messages.strandedReplyRecovery` opt-in surface so guarded recovery is the default for the specific stranded-final class.

## Why This Change Was Made

The July 3 Telegram repro is not a broad final-fallback problem; it is a silent-success problem. In `message_tool_only`, final assistant text is intentionally private, but a substantive final with no message-tool delivery should not end the user-visible source turn as if everything succeeded.

The fix now:

- warns only through the existing substantive private-final predicate;
- skips `room_event`, `sendPolicyDenied`, successful source delivery, short/silent finals, and explicit silence;
- enqueues exactly one retry marked `stranded-reply-retry`;
- applies that recovery to both direct source turns and queued followup turns;
- prepends that retry ahead of already queued follow-ups, protects it from old-item overflow eviction, drains it before overflow summaries, and uses the refreshed follow-up runner;
- stores retry identity in private queued-run metadata rather than user-controlled summary text;
- forces that retry out of collect batching and suppresses retry prompt persistence;
- asks the model to deliver the sanitized visible reply via `message(action=send)`;
- if enqueueing fails or the retry strands again, delivers only a marked sanitized diagnostic;
- suppresses that diagnostic only when the retry already delivered to the source chat through the message tool or internal source-reply path;
- never marks or auto-delivers the original private final text.

## User Impact

For users in Telegram/source-channel chats configured for tool-only visible replies, a substantive reply that previously disappeared should now either:

- recover through one visible `message(action=send)` retry, or
- show `I generated a reply but could not deliver it to this chat. Please try again.`

Intentional silence remains silent. Hidden reasoning, tool output, trace text, raw private finals, send-policy-denied text, room events, and short notes are not auto-published.

target.title: fix(gateway): reduce inline avatar size cap from 2 MB to 256 KB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`agents.list` inlines each agent's avatar as a base64 `data:` URL with a per-avatar cap of 2 MB (`AVATAR_MAX_BYTES`). Images carrying embedded metadata (C2PA provenance manifests, etc.) can easily hit that cap, ballooning the response.

- **Observed**: 3 agents with PNG avatars → **4.15 MB `agents.list` response** (one avatar carried an embedded C2PA manifest).
- **Projected**: 10 such agents → ~20 MB in a single RPC response.
- **Impact**: Android client's default request timeout (15 s) was too short to receive a multi-MB `agents.list`, leaving the agent list empty on slow links. Mitigated client-side in #103248, but that's not a fix.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix (performance regression)
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related to #103265
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

`AVATAR_MAX_BYTES = 2 MB` was too generous for inline avatar data URLs. Each agent's avatar is read in full and base64-encoded with no downscaling or metadata stripping. A single ~2 MB PNG produces a ~2.7 MB base64 string, and three such avatars dominate the response. Lowering the cap to 256 KB — consistent with the existing `GITHUB_AVATAR_MAX_BYTES` (256 KB) — keeps the response bounded while remaining generous for UI thumbnails.

When an avatar file exceeds the cap, `resolveIdentityAvatarUrl` returns `undefined` (avatar not displayed, no error) and emits a `logWarn` so operators can identify which agent's avatar was skipped. The Control UI upload path already reads the same `AVATAR_MAX_BYTES` constant, so oversized uploads are rejected immediately at upload time.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: agents.list response size with photo avatars
- **Real environment tested**: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/avatar-cap-103265` at origin/main HEAD

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```typescript
// Verification: AVATAR_MAX_BYTES constant updated
import { AVATAR_MAX_BYTES } from "./src/shared/avatar-policy.ts";
console.log(AVATAR_MAX_BYTES); // 262144 (256 KB)
```

**Previous cap**: 2,097,152 bytes (2 MB) → base64 overhead ~33% → ~2.8 MB wire per avatar
**New cap**:      262,144 bytes (256 KB) → base64 overhead ~33% → ~349 KB wire per avatar

| Scenario | Before (wire per avatar) | After (wire per avatar) |
|----------|:------------------------:|:-----------------------:|
| Small avatar (32 KB PNG) | ~43 KB | ~43 KB (unchanged) |
| Medium avatar (128 KB PNG) | ~171 KB | ~171 KB (unchanged) |
| Large avatar (2 MB PNG + C2PA) | ~2.7 MB | ✅ rejected (undefined) |
| 3 × large avatars | ~8 MB `agents.list` | ~1 MB `agents.list` |

**Full test suite (avatar-related, gateway session-utils):**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-avatar.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```
```console
✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-avatar.test.ts > ... > rejects local avatars larger than max bytes 3ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  13 passed (13)
```

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```
```console
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  476 passed (476)
```

**Test output confirms**:
1. `resolveAgentAvatar` correctly rejects files over the new cap
2. All existing session utility tests pass with no regression
3. Oversized avatars emit a `logWarn` (verified by code path: `matchRootFileOpenFailure` returns `"too-large"` → `logWarn` with agent ID and file path)

**What was NOT tested**: Live gateway RPC over WebSocket with real oversized avatars (the cap change is exercised by unit tests; the avatar-undefined fallback is existing behavior proven by the `openRootFileSync` rejection path).

## Root Cause

`src/shared/avatar-policy.ts` set `AVATAR_MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024` without distinguishing between the full-resolution image (suitable for disk) and the inline data URL representation (which should be a thumbnail). No downscaling, compression, or metadata stripping was applied before base64 encoding.

**Files changed**:
- `src/shared/avatar-policy.ts` — cap 2 MB → 256 KB (1 line)
- `src/gateway/session-utils.ts` — `logWarn` on oversized avatar skip + `matchRootFileOpenFailure` import (12 lines)

## Alternatives Considered

This PR takes the minimal cap-reduction approach. Two other options were scoped but deferred:

1. **Resize/re-encode with sharp**: Would apply lossy compression to bring every avatar under ~64 KB regardless of source. Deferred because `sharp` is a native C++ dependency with `pnpm install` compilation overhead — better scoped to a separate change if maintainers want it.
2. **Lazy fetch endpoint (`agents.avatar` RPC)**: `agents.list` would return a reference URI instead of the inline data URL, and clients would fetch avatars lazily. Architecturally cleaner but requires client-side changes on Android, Web UI, and Desktop simultaneously. This server-only fix works immediately for all clients.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing sandboxed file-read boundary unchanged
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrows the accepted sizes

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — reduces the ceiling; avatars under 256 KB are unaffected. Previously-working >256 KB avatars become `undefined` (not displayed) without error.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix for this PR**: Yes — the tightest correct change with zero architectural risk. It does not prevent every large response, but it sets a sane ceiling that matches the existing GitHub preview limit.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternatives considered**: See table above; the two richer fixes are scoped but left for separate PRs if maintainers prefer them.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

---

target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try it:** this is the foundation (Workspaces UI + builtins). Check out **#101098** to run the whole feature in one branch; the default *Overview-as-data* workspace renders on first load.

---

# Control UI: Workspaces tab — live grid, built-in widgets, Overview-as-data (2/3)

> **The dashboard your agent builds with you.** This is where the workspace document from #101094 becomes the whole trusted dashboard experience: a live tab strip, a drag/drop grid, nine built-in widgets, and a default Overview that's no longer hand-coded markup but the same document everything else in this series composes — all live, no reload, ever.

![End-to-end: the Overview-as-data default workspace, then an agent composing a Financials tab live with no reload, a pending custom widget approved and mounted, live data pushes, and the operator dragging, collapsing, and using the cell menu — all against the same document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/dashboard-demo.gif)

*▶ Full-quality recording ([light](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/modular-dashboard-demo-v1/dashboard-demo.mp4) / [dark](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/modular-dashboard-demo-v1/dashboard-demo-dark.mp4)).*

> **Stack note.** This is #101097 of a three-PR stack (#101094 backend → #101097 here → #101098 custom widgets). The reviewable new work in *this* PR is the UI layer — **review #101094 first.** Because we don't have upstream write access to set GitHub-native stacked bases, all three PRs target `main` with cumulative diffs, so this branch's diff includes #101094's commits until it merges to `main`; read the new `ui/` files and the five small core edits below as the delta.

## What problem this solves

#101094 gives the document and the control plane; this PR gives operators somewhere to see it, touch it, and use it on day one. Small-business operators need drag/drop, hide/collapse, and a layout that's actually useful the moment they open it — no widget-building required. Maintainers need the same operational picture the current Overview page gives them (cost, sessions, cron, activity, instance health), just now expressed as workspace content they can rearrange and extend, and they need to see, live, when an agent has changed something — with the ability to immediately push back with their own drag/drop, on the exact same document.

Shipping the grid and the content together, in one PR, is the point: an empty grid isn't a product, and a set of widgets with nowhere to live isn't either. This is the PR where the default Control UI experience actually changes.

## What's in this PR

**The shell — tab strip, grid, interaction:**
- **One new Control UI tab, "Workspaces"** — registered through the plugin-tab descriptor + `BUNDLED_TAB_VIEWS` mechanism #99930 just introduced for logbook. This is the second consumer of that seam, not a new one.
- **Live workspace tab strip** rendered from `workspace.json`, honoring saved tab order, with hidden tabs in an overflow menu. Deep-linkable (`?plugin=dashboard&id=workspaces&ws=<slug>`) — back/forward and reload preserve the active tab.
- **12-column CSS grid** with hand-rolled pointer-based drag/drop and resize (no new grid dependency) — drag a widget, see a ghost preview snapped to the grid, drop, and the layout persists via the gateway RPC with optimistic local update + revert-on-failure.
- **Collapse / hide / remove / move-to-tab** from each widget's cell menu, all persisted through the same RPC surface #101094 shipped.
- **Per-cell error boundaries** — if a widget throws, only that cell shows an error card; the rest of the grid, and every other tab, is unaffected.
- **Provenance chips** — widgets created by an agent show a small "AI" badge with the agent id on hover. This is a feature, not an afterthought: operators should see what their agent built, at a glance.
- **Live updates** — the view subscribes to `plugin.dashboard.changed` and refetches (or falls back to a short poll if push events aren't available on a given connection path — the PR states explicitly which one shipped).

**The content — nine built-in widgets, and a real default workspace:**
- **9 built-in, trusted widgets**, rendered as Lit templates directly inside the Control UI (not sandboxed — these ship with the plugin, they're not agent-authored code):
  - `stat-card` — big number + label + optional delta
  - `markdown` — static or file-bound markdown body
  - `table` — compact rows + count footer
  - `iframe-embed` — embedded URL, respecting the existing embed-sandbox and external-URL policy exactly as chat embeds do today
  - `sessions` — latest sessions with live-run indicator
  - `usage` — cost/tokens mini-summary
  - `cron` — next runs + last status per job
  - `instances` — connected instances + health
  - `activity` — recent activity feed
- **Overview-as-data**: the default `main` workspace ships as a seeded `workspace.json` (`createdBy: "system"`) — usage + instance-health cards, sessions + cron side by side, activity feed below. It reads the same at 1280px and reflows to single-column below ~900px. This replaces the old hand-coded Overview page with the same information, expressed as workspace content instead of markup.
- Each widget is a **thin re-implementation against existing read RPCs** (sessions/usage/cron/instances/activity) — deliberately not reusing the current page view functions, which are welded to their own pages' state. Every RPC method a builtin can call is frozen into an explicit allowlist, enforced at schema-validation time in #101094's store.
- Loading / empty / error states on every widget, inside its own cell — nothing here can throw past the per-cell boundary this PR's shell provides.
- Polling hygiene: refresh piggybacks on the document-change broadcast for layout edits, plus a modest per-widget interval for data refresh that stops the moment the tab isn't visible (no orphan timers).

Shell and content share one lifecycle here on purpose: the grid's error boundary is what makes the widget set safe to ship as "always on," and the widget set is what makes the grid worth landing as the new default rather than an opt-in extra.

## See it

**Overview-as-data — the default workspace, light and dark:**

![Overview-as-data default workspace, light theme — nine live builtins: cost and token cards, instance health, sessions, cron ok/error, and the activity feed, all reading live RPCs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/01-overview-live-builtins.png)

![The same Overview-as-data workspace in the dark theme, adopting the #99289 palette without any per-theme markup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/overview-dark.png)

**An agent composing a tab live, and human interaction on the composed grid:**

![An agent composing a Financials tab live in an already-open browser — overlay chips show the dashboard.tab.create / dashboard.widget.add RPCs firing; the tab strip updates with no reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/02-financials-tab-appears-live.png)

![The composed dashboard under human control — a widget cell's kebab menu open (hide / remove / move-to-tab / collapse), escaping its card cleanly over the 12-column grid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/06-menu-collapse-composed-dashboard.png)

## How it works

The whole surface is one bundled Control-UI tab. There is no new UI mechanism here — this is the *second* consumer of the plugin-tab seam #99930 introduced for logbook.

### From plugin descriptor to a native bundled view

`extensions/dashboard` registers a single tab descriptor:

```ts
api.session.controls.registerControlUiDescriptor({
  surface: "tab", id: "workspaces", label: "Workspaces",
  group: "control", requiredScopes: ["operator.read"],
});
```

That descriptor is projected into the per-connection hello `controlUiTabs` payload (scope-filtered, so the tab is hidden for connections lacking `operator.read`). The Control UI already knows how to render a *bundled* view for a plugin tab: this PR adds one entry to the `BUNDLED_TAB_VIEWS` map in `plugin-page.ts` keyed `"dashboard/workspaces"`, whose lazy import returns our render + stop functions. No descriptor `path` is set, so the descriptor's generic iframe branch never triggers — the tab renders as first-party Lit, not a sandboxed page.

The page itself follows workboard's three-way split, because the controller is stateful: a thin `LitElement` page (`@consume(applicationContext)` + subscription lifecycle), a pure `dashboard-view.ts` render layer, and a `lib/dashboard/` controller that owns data and grid logic.

### The 12-column grid and hand-rolled drag/drop

The grid is plain CSS grid, 12 columns, widgets absolutely placed by `grid-column`/`grid-row` spans from their doc coordinates. Drag/drop and resize are **hand-rolled pointer-event math in `lib/dashboard/grid.ts`** — deliberately no `gridstack`/`interact.js`, per the repo's lean-deps rule, because snap-to-grid and a ghost preview are simple enough not to justify a dependency. A drag shows a ghost snapped to the grid; on drop the layout updates optimistically and persists via `dashboard.widget.move` / `dashboard.widget.setLayout`; an RPC failure reverts the local state. Overlapping drops are rejected with a nearest-free-slot fallback rather than silently stacking cells.

Collapse, hide, remove, and move-to-tab all live in each cell's kebab menu and persist through the same #101094 RPC surface — this PR **adds no new mutation path**, only a renderer and an interaction layer over the existing store.

### Live updates and the per-cell error boundary

The view subscribes to `plugin.dashboard.changed` on the gateway client and refetches on a version bump (skipping its own echo) — the push path is what shipped (the Control UI's WS client surfaces event frames), with a short poll retained only as a fallback. This is what makes the agent's edits appear live in an already-open browser with no reload.

Every widget render is wrapped in a **per-cell error boundary**: if a widget throws, only that cell shows an error card — the rest of the grid, and every other tab, is untouched. That boundary is precisely what makes it safe to ship the widget set as always-on rather than opt-in, and it's what PR3's sandboxed custom widgets mount inside.

### Builtins bind to read RPCs through an allowlist

The 9 builtins (`stat-card`, `markdown`, `table`, `iframe-embed`, `sessions`, `usage`, `cron`, `instances`, `activity`) are trusted first-party Lit templates — there is no sandboxing story here because nothing is agent- or user-authored HTML (that's PR3). Each data widget is a **thin re-implementation against an existing read RPC**, deliberately *not* reusing the current page view functions, which are welded to their own pages' state. The RPCs a builtin may call are frozen into an explicit allowlist, enforced at schema-validation time in #101094's store — a widget gets a named door, not an open one. `iframe-embed` is the only widget that touches an external URL, and it reuses the existing embed-sandbox / external-URL config the Control UI already enforces for chat embeds — no new policy surface.

### Overview-as-data

The default `main` workspace ships as a seeded `workspace.json` (`createdBy: "system"`): usage + instance-health cards, sessions and cron side by side, activity below. It reflows to single-column under ~900px. This replaces the old hand-coded Overview page with the *same information expressed as workspace content* — so the redesign goals from #77774 / #86460 become arrangeable content instead of a second hand-coded page.

### The core footprint — evidence of a lean core

The entire diff to core `ui/` is **five existing files**, all small additive edits:

- `ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-page.ts` — one `BUNDLED_TAB_VIEWS` entry;
- `ui/src/styles.css` — one stylesheet import;
- a breadcrumb-label prop threaded through `ui/src/app/app-host.ts`, `ui/src/components/app-topbar.ts`, and `ui/src/components/dashboard-header.ts` (a generic improvement — every plugin tab, e.g. logbook, gets a proper breadcrumb label, not just this one).

Everything else is *new* files under `ui/src/pages/plugin/dashboard-*`, `ui/src/lib/dashboard/`, and `ui/src/components/dashboard-widget-cell.ts`. No new UI framework, no new grid library, no new npm dependency — the Lit shell stays exactly as it is.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** The Control UI is a fixed set of hand-coded views — an operator (or an agent acting for them) cannot arrange their own dashboard. This PR adds the bundled "Workspaces" Control-UI tab: a live 12-column grid with hand-rolled drag/drop and resize, 9 trusted built-in widgets, and the Overview-as-data default workspace, all rendered from `workspace.json` and live-updating on `plugin.dashboard.changed` with no reload.

**Evidence:** 246 dashboard unit/browser tests pass (grid math including overlap-rejection with nearest-free-slot fallback, the workboard-style controller/lib split, widget-cell chrome + the per-cell error boundary), plus the mocked-gateway E2E scenarios and a clean `pnpm ui:build`. The rendered result — Overview-as-data in light and dark, an agent composing a Financials tab live with the `dashboard.*` RPCs firing, and human drag/collapse/menu interaction on the composed grid — is in the screenshots above and the recording on the tracking issue.

## Verification

**Size — why the diff looks big but isn't:** GitHub shows ~14K changed lines, but the reviewable **source** is ~4,000 lines across 23 files. The remainder is 61 generated i18n locale-bundle files (regenerated by `pnpm ui:i18n:sync`, never hand-edited — English source lives in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`) plus tests. The hand-written UI-source increment is well under VISION.md's ~5K reviewable-line guideline.

- Unit tests for grid math (snap-to-grid, overlap rejection with nearest-free-slot fallback) and the dashboard controller/lib split.
- Component/browser tests for the widget cell (collapse, menu actions, error-boundary rendering).
- Data-shape mapping unit tests per widget (RPC payload fixture in, rendered model out).
- E2E scenarios: drag/resize/collapse/hide persisting through reload, live-update on a broadcast event, the broken-widget isolation case (sibling cells and other tabs unaffected), all 9 builtins with mocked data asserting loading/empty/error states render correctly.
- `iframe-embed` sandbox-mode × internal/external URL matrix tested against the existing embed policy.
- Default-workspace seed test: fresh state dir produces the documented layout; visual screenshot check light+dark.
- Timer-lifecycle test: polling stops when the Workspaces tab is left (no orphan intervals).
- `pnpm ui:i18n:check` and `pnpm ui:build` clean; no new `ui/` dependencies.
- The dashboard UI suites pass (246 unit/browser tests across `lib/dashboard`, the plugin page, and the widget cells), plus the mocked-gateway E2E scenarios and `ui:build`. CI runs on this PR.

## Closes / part of

Closes **#66138** ("make OpenClaw feel like WordPress" — this is the modular, plugin-driven surface that issue asked for). Supersedes **#77774** / **#86460** (the competing Overview redesign proposals) by making that content a workspace document instead of a second hand-coded page — the redesign goals those issues wanted become workspace content, arrangeable like everything else. Partially addresses **#72545** (exec-approvals surface — activity/cron widgets surface this operational picture, though a dedicated approvals widget is future work) and **#76089** (spawn-subagent button — the `sendPrompt` bridge capability lands in #101098, but the sessions/activity widgets here are the visibility half of that story). Part of #101093. Depends on #101094. Precedes #101098.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #94705. Supersedes #94735 because its stale fork branch could not safely accept the current-main maintainer refactor.

With `models.mode: "replace"`, the default `openclaw models list` output still appended models from authenticated providers that were absent from `models.providers`. That contradicted replace-mode configuration semantics and made the configured-model list look broader than the effective configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The authenticated-catalog append helper now reads the canonical config directly and returns early in replace mode. This keeps the policy at the row source that introduces the leak, avoids threading a derived boolean through the row-building context, and leaves explicit `--all` and `--provider` browsing on their existing source-plan paths.

The regression coverage exercises both merge and replace semantics, proves replace mode skips the authenticated catalog entirely, and separately protects explicit all/provider browsing. The replacement commit preserves original contributor credit for @Monkey-wusky.

## User Impact

`openclaw models list` now shows only explicitly configured provider models when `models.mode` is `replace`. Users can still browse the complete catalog with `--all` or narrow catalog browsing with `--provider`.

## Evidence

- Current-main source audit: the default configured-list path is the only caller of the authenticated-catalog append helper; explicit all/provider paths use the source planner and remain unaffected.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox baseline on original exact head `bb6a70e0c257cd2213670478156a638cc1c5ac97`: `src/commands/models.list.e2e.test.ts` passed 20/20 (`run_59f7ce52973a`).

target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint after inbound admission gates pass. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

When the first cold turn has no stored thread session entry yet, the monitor now records a pending backfill marker and adopts it once `recordInboundSessionMeta` creates the stored session id. That keeps the marker stable for same-session follow-ups and failed-fetch no-retry, without blocking a later real session-id rotation.

Backfilled sender labels use stable Mattermost user ids instead of per-post user lookups, keeping recovery bounded to the thread fetch path.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(gateway): prevent credential-mutation barrier from blocking all requests indefinitely
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a credential-mutating gateway method (`device.pair.remove`, `device.token.rotate`, `device.token.revoke`, `node.pair.remove`) is being dispatched, a barrier is set that blocks **all subsequent requests** on that WebSocket connection until the dispatch settles. If the dispatch hangs for any reason, the `for(;;)` barrier loop blocks every following request forever — the connection appears dead and requires a gateway restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

The realistic deadlock chain (all links confirmed by source inspection):

```
withLock (no-timeout mutex, @openclaw/fs-safe/async-lock.js:17)
  └─ rotateDeviceToken acquires lock at device-pairing.ts:1431
     └─ I/O stall / DB deadlock inside lock → lock never released
        └─ handleGatewayRequest never returns
           └─ barrier never cleared
              └─ for(;;) loop blocks ALL subsequent WS requests
                 └─ Connection dead — only gateway restart fixes it
```

The barrier wait had **no timeout**, so a single stuck credential-mutation handler could permanently DoS the entire WebSocket connection.

## User Impact

Without this fix, any I/O stall or deadlock inside a credential-mutating handler causes the affected WebSocket connection to silently stop processing requests. The gateway appears connected but ignores all inbound RPCs until restarted.

## Evidence

**Unit tests (6/6 passed):**

```
 ✓ credential-mutation barrier timeout > does not delay requests when barrier resolves quickly 294ms
 ✓ credential-mutation barrier timeout > unblocks via timeout when barrier never settles 506ms
 ✓ credential-mutation barrier timeout > does not throw when barrier rejects 2ms
 ✓ credential-mutation barrier timeout > exits loop when isClosed returns true 256ms
 ✓ credential-mutation barrier timeout > breaks out of loop when barrier becomes undefined 2ms
 ✓ credential-mutation barrier timeout > re-checks barrier after timeout in case new barrier was set 254ms
```

**Live deadlock chain proof (transient, not committed):**

All 7 checks passed:

1. `withLock`: second call blocked 501ms (no timeout) ✅
2. Barrier blocked 5 iterations × 200ms without breaking ✅
3. Barrier never cleared by stuck dispatch ✅
4. `device-pairing.ts`: `withLock = createAsyncLock()` ✅
5. `device-pairing.ts`: `rotateDeviceToken` uses `await withLock(...)` ✅
6. Fix: 30s timeout unblocks after 2 iterations ✅
7. Fix: connection recovers after timeout ✅

**Proof method:** Used `@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced` `createAsyncLock` directly to verify the mutex has no timeout. Simulated the full barrier + timeout pattern with a never-settling Promise. Proof script is transient — not committed to the repo.

> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try this PR:** with ≥2 agents/operators — group the tab strip by agent, mark a tab **private**, and watch presence → a private tab is **absent server-side** from a non-owner's payload (fail-closed); live "who's viewing" presence.

---

# Dashboard: control hub — per-agent nesting, shared/private tabs, presence

> The multi-agent, multi-operator half of the vision: organize the dashboard by which agent built what, keep some tabs private, and see who else is in the workspace live.

Closes #101151, #101152, #101153. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff.

## What's in this PR
- **Per-agent nesting (#101151)** — group the tab strip by each tab's `createdBy` provenance, with a collapse/expand control to fold a whole agent's tabs away. Pure grouping over existing provenance.
- **Shared/private tabs (#101152)** — a tab may be `private`, visible only to its owner (enforced server-side, below).
- **Presence (#101153)** — a lightweight "who's viewing this tab" indicator over the existing broadcast path; the presence event carries `{ operator, tabSlug, at }` (id + tab only, never document state), ephemeral and never persisted.

## Security (private tabs)
Visibility is enforced **server-side**, not by hiding in the UI: every gateway response that serializes the workspace doc passes through `filterWorkspaceForOperator(doc, resolveOperatorIdentity(client))` (a `respondDoc` helper on `workspace.get`, every mutation response, `tab.create`, and `undo`), so a private tab the caller doesn't own is absent from the wire payload **and** the tab order. The store keeps the full doc; only the response is filtered. **Fail-closed:** an unidentified operator sees zero private tabs. (Operator identity is currently keyed on the paired **device id** — documented as the exact seam where a richer per-human identity threads in; a bootstrap-authed connection with no paired device can neither see nor own a private tab.)

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** With many agents and/or operators sharing one dashboard, there was no way to organize by agent, keep a tab private, or see concurrent activity. This adds per-agent grouping, server-enforced private tabs, and live presence.
**Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` → 90 passed (visibility filter, fail-closed default, owner-only access, presence-payload shape — a private tab owned by A verified absent from B's serialized payload and tab order); `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/pages/plugin` → 119 passed (actor grouping/fold, presence store TTL + self-exclusion, visibility round-trip); `ui:i18n:check`, `ui:build`, full type-aware oxlint clean.

target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof #2 — the production failure class, rescued (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch, isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message: a deep-research skill task that fanned out **8 investigators in two batches** (5-concurrency staggering, one spawn attempt failed and was retried by the parent), each writing a multi-section report over ~5 minutes. This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

```
14:34:41  user sends the research task                        [the ONLY user message]
14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion
          announces exhaust retries and give up ("completion agent did not produce a
          visible reply") — the parent NO_REPLYs essentially every completion event.
          On unpatched openclaw this session is now permanently parked.
14:53:01  last child settles → drain
14:53:02  settle wake attempt 1 dispatched; its turn begins "All 8 investigators have
          now reported… Writing the final report" → provider stream stalls mid-
          synthesis → run dies (LLM request timed out) at 14:55:21
14:55:31  hardening retry (`…:retry-1` key, 30 s backoff) → wake turn runs 4.7 min →
15:00:16  completes, delivering the FULL ~48,000-char final report into the session
14:59:31  precautionary attempt 3 (`…:retry-2`, dispatched while attempt 2's RPC await
          timed out) → queued turn replies NO_REPLY (report already delivered) — the
          escape hatch bounds duplicates
```

Consolidated report delivered with **0 post-yield user messages**, through eight announce give-ups AND a dead first wake turn. The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: fix(sessions): guard sessions.create fork against cross-plugin ownership bypass
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  8 passed | 48 skipped (56)
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`); live gateway RPC over WebSocket transport

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed)

# Dashboard: apps layer — full-bleed tabs + widget gallery

> Two steps toward "every tab is a web app": a tab can be a single full-bleed widget, and widgets can be browsed and installed from a registry — through the same approval gate and sandbox as any custom widget.

Closes #101148 and #101149. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the full-bleed layout + gallery pieces as the delta.

## What's in this PR
- **Full-bleed tab (#101148)** — a tab may set `layout: "full"`, rendering a single widget filling the content area with no grid chrome; a menu toggle flips it. A custom widget can now *be* the tab — a real app surface.
- **Widget gallery + install-from-URL (#101149)** — browse a registry `index.json`, see the capabilities a widget requests, and install it. The gallery is the third-party-code surface, so it's deliberately conservative: **install is client-fetch only** — the gateway never receives or fetches a URL (a source-scan guard test asserts no `fetch`/`https` in the install path), so there is no server-side SSRF; the bundle is capped (512 KB, ≤64 files), path-jailed, extension-allowlisted, and run through the existing `validateWidgetManifest`; requested capabilities are surfaced *before* install.
